items.statement: Every one of the six named carbocation models has an explicit computational status, method, common energy reference and validation record, including failures.
items.expected: Six model records are present and individually identifiable; no model is silently omitted.

items.statement: Advanced transition-state candidates are supported by a first-order-saddle diagnostic and bidirectional IRC or a specifically justified alternative connectivity check.
items.expected: Each advanced candidate retains validation context tied to its candidate and parent model.

items.statement: The short-chain C10 alpha model is not supported as a stable isolated minimum and is reported as rearranging or otherwise failing to remain alpha-like.
items.expected: C10_alpha status and conclusion indicate instability/rearrangement, with evidence and limitations.

items.statement: For C15 and C17, alpha-like carbocation pathways support direct dehydrogenation to olefin more favorably than the corresponding short-chain behavior.
items.expected: The submitted comparison identifies stabilized long-chain alpha behavior and direct dehydrogenation as favored within its stated model scope.
